title: RBAC V2: permissions model, audit schema & SIEM export rollout
content:
Purpose
This doc captures the current RBAC v2 design proposal with a focus on permissions model changes, the audit/event schema we\u2019ll emit, evidence automation requirements for compliance review, and a pragmatic rollout plan including SIEM export. It is a living working doc for Security, Infra, SRE, and Product to iterate on before creating the formal spec.

Goals (non-exhaustive)
- Provide fine-grained, attribute-aware permissions that map to product surfaces (API, Console, Dedicated, Private).
- Ensure audit logs contain sufficient contextual evidence for compliance (who, what, where, why, outcome).
- Enable automated evidence collection and retention for SOC audits and customer compliance requests.
- Streamline SIEM export to support customer-managed detection & response and internal security monitoring.
- Minimize disruption: phased rollout with compatibility fallbacks and migration tooling.

High-level design notes
1) Permissions model (concepts)
- Principals: users, service-accounts, groups, external-identity-roles (OIDC/SAML mapped).
- Resources: hierarchical resource model (organization > workspace > project > model-endpoint > route).
- Actions: verbs (read/list, write/create, execute/invoke, configure, admin).
- Constraints/conditions: attribute-based checks (time-window, source-ip, network-zone, billing-account, data-class).
- Bindings: allow multiple bindings per principal with OR semantics; support deny rules with higher precedence.
- Permission evaluation: lowest-latency path in runtime, precompiled policy cache per node with incremental invalidation.

2) Example permission binding (text form)
- binding_id: b-1245
- principal: group:ml-platform@redwood.ai
- resource: workspace:acme > project:search-relevancy
- action: invoke:model.generate
- condition: request.source_ip in 10.4.0.0/14 AND request.time between 09:00-18:00 UTC
(note: the above is for human-readability; the wire format is ACL proto we maintain in the rbac-proto repo)

3) Audit/event schema (required fields)
We propose a JSON event envelope with the following top-level string fields (all values as strings or arrays):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO-8601)
- event_type (authz_check | authz_grant | authz_denied | config_change | data_access | admin_action | system_error)
- principal_id (user|service|group)
- principal_identity_source (okta|github|sso|internal)
- action (explicit verb, e.g., model.invoke, route.update)
- resource_id (canonical resource path)
- resource_type (model_endpoint|route|workspace|project|org)
- outcome (allowed|denied|error)
- request_id (trace id matching request path)
- client_ip
- region
- request_payload_hash (sha256)
- response_status (http status or internal code)
- decision_source (local-cache|policy-service|fallback)
- policy_snapshot_id (id of policy commit used during decision)
- evidence_refs (list of evidence IDs collected for this event)
- human_reason (optional free text when admin overrides)

Minimal vs enriched modes
- Minimal: fields above only; retention cheap, used for SIEM initial ingest.
- Enriched: append contextual blobs (policy dump, user session metadata, model config, full request metadata) stored separately as evidence artifacts referenced from evidence_refs. Enriched mode used for compliance requests and internal investigations.

4) Evidence automation model
- Evidence artifacts: signed, time-stamped blobs (JSON/plaintext) stored in customer-segmented audit buckets. Each artifact is referenced by evidence_id and includes metadata: creator, created_at, type, retention_tier.
- Auto-capture triggers: admin actions, any denied authz_check, data access to sensitive datasets, model-config changes, routing/pinning updates, and periodic snapshots (daily policy snapshot).
- Retention policy: default 90d in cheap tier, 1y in compliance tier, configurable per-customer (for Private deployments).
- Access controls: evidence buckets are encrypted and ACL\u2019d; evidence retrieval requires a separate audit_evidence:read permission and must be logged.

5) SIEM export requirements
- Two export channels: internal security stream (high-volume minimal events) and customer-managed export (filtered, delivered to customer SIEM endpoint).
- Transport: OTLP/HTTP to collector, support for Syslog forwarding, Kinesis/SQS for high-throughput customers.
- Schema mapping: ensure field renames are documented and present a stable mapping table to Splunk/Elastic/QRadar ingestion teams.
- Backpressure handling: batch and drop-priority labeling (critical|error|audit|telemetry) to avoid outages.
- Verification: signed sample stream for customer acceptance testing; replay capability for last 7 days.

Migration and rollout plan (phased)
Phase 0 — Finalize spec and small-scale prototype (Q4 2025)\- Complete wire-format proto definitions and Confluence spec.\- Small prototype of policy-service and local runtime cache in staging.\- Security review and threat model.

Phase 1 — Internal opt-in & infra plumbing (Q1 2026)\- Allow internal teams to opt-in to RBAC v2 in non-prod workspaces.\- Start sending audit events (minimal mode) to internal SIEM.\- Build evidence artifact store with encryption and retention tiers.\- Migrate infra to emit policy_snapshot_id for decision traceability.

Phase 2 — Beta with select customers (Q2 2026)\- Offer RBAC v2 as beta flag for Hosted API customers who request fine-grained controls.\- Customer SIEM export pilot (2 customers) with signed samples and mapping doc.\- Run a red-team style verification of evidence integrity and access controls.

Phase 3 — Default for new orgs + opt-in migration tooling (Q3 2026)\- New orgs created after cutover default to RBAC v2.\- Provide migration tools to convert role mappings from v1 -> v2 (best-effort mappings).\- Offer a compatibility mode where v1 tokens are evaluated by wrapper layer that depends on v2 policy mapping.

Phase 4 — Hard cutover and enforcement (Q4 2026)\- Full enforcement across hosted and dedicated regions by default.\- Private customers: provide timeline and tools; require explicit opt-in for forced migration when on-prem constraints require special handling.

Operational concerns & performance
- Latency SLO: authz check must be < 2ms p50 for cached decisions; policy-service cold checks target < 10ms p50. Implement prefetching of per-workspace policy in node startup.
- Policy size constraints: reduction strategies (policy templating, condition decomposition) so runtime cache size stays bounded.
- Observability: histogram metrics for policy evaluation time, cache hit rate, denied-rate by resource, top denying policies.
- Rollback safety: runtime supports immediate fallback to v1 policy engine for orgs flagged as problematic.

Implementation TODOs (near-term)
- [ ] Finalize proto fields for audit envelope (owner: Evan).
- [ ] Add policy_snapshot_id emission in policy-service (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Implement evidence store API and signed artifact format (owner: Samir).
- [ ] SIEM export adapters: Splunk & Elastic MVP (owner: Jules).
- [ ] End-to-end test harness that simulates migration scenarios (owner: Marisol).
- [ ] Customer communication templates and migration checklist for Solutions Engineering (owner: Product Ops).

Open questions / trade-offs (for discussion)
- Deny rules: do we allow org-level deny rules that affect centralized infra? Precedence model needs strong testing.
- Policy language: Rego vs custom DSL vs proto AST. Rego offers expressivity but may be heavy for low-latency checks.
- Evidence retention: what is reasonable default for Hosted to balance cost and auditability? Proposed 90d cheapest tier but need feedback from Compliance.
- SIEM quotas: what is the default sampling policy for high-volume orgs to avoid excessive cost?

Security review checklist (pre-rollout)
- Threat model signed off and mitigations tracked.
- Evidence store encryption keys rotated and managed via KMS.
- Access gating for evidence retrieval (separate permission) and MFA enforcement for high-privilege actions.
- Integrity: sign artifacts with service key and store verification metadata in ledger for tamper detection.

Customer-facing migration notes (draft text)
- Summary: RBAC v2 adds attribute-aware, fine-grained control and richer audit evidence exports. We will provide migration tooling and compatibility modes to minimize downtime. Beta customers can opt-in starting Q2.
- What to expect: slightly different role semantics (more granular); new permissions to control evidence access and SIEM exports; recommended review of existing groups/roles to map to new bindings.

Appendix: sample event (minimal)
{\n  "event_id": "f0a1e3d4-9c88-4b12-b3a1-137c8c9f6a10",\n  "timestamp": "2025-10-11T15:12:03Z",\n  "event_type": "authz_check",\n  "principal_id": "user:elaine@acme.com",\n  "principal_identity_source": "okta",\n  "action": "model.invoke",\n  "resource_id": "org:acme/workspace:search/project:prod/models/gpt-11/endpoint:alpha",\n  "resource_type": "model_endpoint",\n  "outcome": "denied",\n  "request_id": "trace-430b1a",\n  "client_ip": "52.24.123.8",\n  "region": "us-west-2",\n  "request_payload_hash": "sha256:abcd...",\n  "response_status": "403",\n  "decision_source": "policy-service",\n  "policy_snapshot_id": "ps-20251011-12",\n  "evidence_refs": ["e-20251011-001"]\n}

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working doc: expect iterative edits. Please comment on the policy precedence section and evidence retention recommendations.
- If you are owning a TODO above, add your name in the TODO line and update linked_artifacts with PRs or tickets as you work them.

End of doc.
